title: Word Problems with Parentheses
intro: Use the contents of one box to explain parentheses.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Combine the two amounts inside one box before multiplying by the number of boxes. Match the expression to the model.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Every box has the same two quantities.

Box 1
3 red
5 blue
Box 2
3 red
5 blue
Box 3
3 red
5 blue
Box 4
3 red
5 blue

(3 + 5) × 4 = 8 × 4 = 32 counters

The parentheses describe one complete box. The factor 4 repeats that whole box.

Ask your student

What does the expression inside the parentheses represent?

If your student needs help

If the student multiplies only one part of the box, have them point to both parts in every box.

Choosing and using the worksheet

These four-problem worksheets use 1–12 counters of each color and 2–9 equal boxes. The calculations are intentionally small enough to focus attention on grouping and meaning. Ask for an expression and an explanation before checking the total.
